metadata.title: Product Bricks & Streams
metadata.description: Buildable, ownable capabilities of Booking Holdings' enterprise applications and financial systems landscape: finance core, money movement, enterprise applications, close and controls, finance data and integration, and architecture governance.

rootGroups.name: Global Finance Core
rootGroups.description: The single book of record: ledger, master data, entities and the high-volume subledger and revenue engines that convert bookings into accounting.

subGroups.name: Ledger and Accounting Core
subGroups.description: S/4HANA ledger, Central Finance, chart of accounts, entities, intercompany and FX.

bricks.name: General Ledger and Central Finance Hub
bricks.description: The global SAP S/4HANA general ledger, fed through Central Finance from brand and legacy source systems. Booking.com's Financial Systems team has run SAP on HANA, moved to Simple Finance in 2016 and started its S/4HANA journey with Central Finance in 2019 (job postings). This brick is the single book of record for every legal entity: universal journal, ledger approach for US GAAP and local GAAP, period control and the document flow from subledgers into the ledger. Whether the target runtime is SAP RISE is an assumption from a third-party job listing.

Harmonised master data is the precondition for Central Finance replication and for converging Booking.com, Priceline, Agoda, KAYAK and OpenTable finance onto one model. Implemented with a master-data-governance workflow (SAP MDG assumed).

bricks.name: High-Volume Transaction Subledger (FI-CA/BRIM)
bricks.description: Contract-accounting subledger that turns booking, payment, cancellation and commission events into business partner and contract-account postings at booking scale (1,235M room nights in 2025). FI-CA and BRIM appear in Booking.com Financial Systems job postings. It keeps transaction detail out of the general ledger, posts summarised entries, and provides open-item clearing for traveler payments, partner balances and commission receivables.

bricks.name: Revenue Recognition Engine
bricks.description: Applies ASC 606 to merchant and agency transactions: principal-versus-agent judgement, gross versus net presentation, timing at check-in or stay completion, cancellations and refunds, and payment facilitation revenue. Merchant revenues grew to $17,755M in 2025 while agency revenues fell to $7,968M as Booking.com shifted to the merchant model (10-K FY2025), so the engine's rules are the most material revenue judgement in the core.

The brick keeps the liability per booking, links it to funds held by licensed e-money entities, and releases it on stay, cancellation or payout.

bricks.name: Payment Event Ingestion and Normalisation

New local methods (for example the Antom partnership for Asian markets, January 2025) must be ledger-ready before launch. The payments platform itself (checkout, routing, fraud) is upstream and out of scope.
